neighbours.label: word just before an expected 'herd(s)' / animal-group noun: the modifier or determiner in 'vast ___', 'their ___', 'great ___' when grazing animals gather or migrate
fire: Every spring the caribou cross the frozen river in vast herds.
Before the railways came, bison wandered the grasslands in immense herds.
Zebras and antelope gather near the waterhole in large herds.
The nomads moved north each summer, driving their herds before them.
From the ridge we watched elephants moving slowly across the valley in small herds.
Reindeer in Lapland are still managed by families who follow the great herds.
Wild horses once grazed these hills in huge herds.
At dusk the cattle drifted back toward the ranch in scattered herds.
quiet: Every spring the old bear crosses the frozen river alone.
Before the railways came, a lone trapper lived on the grasslands.
A single heron stood near the waterhole all afternoon.
The nomads moved north each summer, carrying their tents on sleds.
From the ridge we watched an eagle circling slowly above the valley.
Salmon in Lapland are still smoked by families who own the old sheds.
A stray dog once slept on these hills beside the chapel.
At dusk the farmer drove back toward the ranch in his truck.

notes: Card: peaks on ' their', ' the', ' great', ' whole', ' were' before herds / migration / herded; + pole promotes ' her', ' his', ' their' (her- continuations), and the - pole fires on 'h' before '-er…'. Probe: 'in enormous [herds]' 0.95, 'in great [numbers]' 0.49, 'in [close family groups]' 0.45, 'his [flock]' 0.29.
